origin.notes: Descriptive pattern name of long, largely anonymous usage.

definition_short: Two or more line pieces stacked on the same file, rank or diagonal, so their force is combined.
definition_long:
Two rooks on a file, a queen behind a rook, a queen behind a bishop on a diagonal. The front piece can capture on a defended square because the rear piece recaptures, and the pair controls the line far more strongly than either alone.

A battery is also the precondition for a discovered attack: put a piece of your own in front of the rear piece and moving it discovers. The queen-plus-bishop diagonal battery aimed at h7 is the standard attacking configuration; three heavy pieces on one file is sometimes called Alekhine's gun.

Recorded as a piece configuration rather than a tactic: a battery does not by itself do anything, it enables things.
epistemic_note: Type D by association, but it is really a configuration that enables motifs rather than a motif that wins material. Flagged so an explanation does not claim a battery is itself the reason a move is good.

preconditions: Two or more friendly line pieces share a file, rank or diagonal with nothing between them
indicators_for: The line points at the enemy king or a weak square
The front piece can capture on a defended square, backed by the rear piece
indicators_against: The line is blocked further along and cannot be opened
The rear piece is more valuable and becomes a target itself

exceptions: Ordering matters: queen in front of rook is usually worse than rook in front of queen, because the more valuable piece meets the defenders first.
limitations: A battery is potential, not achievement. Do not report it as the reason for a move unless the position shows what it actually enables.

explanation_templates.beginner: Two pieces are lined up on the same line, so they work together — the one in front can take, and the one behind takes back.
explanation_templates.intermediate: A battery on the {line}. It doubles the pressure and sets up a discovery if the front piece moves.
explanation_templates.advanced: Battery. Check the ordering — the cheaper piece generally belongs in front.
explanation_templates.hedge: A battery enables tactics rather than being one; say what it actually threatens here.
